case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Appeal No. 58/79, decided on 24 September 1979

clause.text: Every person has the right to apply to the Supreme Court for violations of fundamental rights.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner properly invoked the Supreme Court's jurisdiction under Article 17 to challenge the Bill's provisions as violations of fundamental rights.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner filed a fundamental rights application under Article 17 alleging violations of fundamental rights by the Bill.
case_context.respondent_argument: The State did not dispute the Court's jurisdiction under Article 17 but focused on the merits of the constitutional issues.
key_facts: The petitioner filed the application directly to the Supreme Court under Article 17.
The application challenged the constitutionality of the Essential Public Service Bill.
The Court considered the application appropriate for fundamental rights adjudication.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court accepted jurisdiction under Article 17 to hear the fundamental rights challenge to the Bill. It emphasized the Court's duty to examine the constitutionality of legislation affecting fundamental rights despite Cabinet certification.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court proceeded to analyze the Bill's provisions under fundamental rights jurisprudence, confirming the petitioner's right to apply under Article 17.
principles_established: Article 17 grants every person the right to apply to the Supreme Court for fundamental rights violations.
Cabinet certification under Article 84 does not preclude judicial review of fundamental rights issues.

outcome.holding: The Court accepted the petitioner's application under Article 17 and exercised its jurisdiction to determine the constitutional validity of the Bill's provisions.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 17 is the constitutional basis for the Supreme Court's jurisdiction to hear and decide fundamental rights applications such as the present challenge to the Bill.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: This is a petition to the Supreme Court under Article 121 of the Constitution invoking our jurisdiction in respect of a Bill entitled the Essential Public Services Bill. The Court has a duty to examine the Bill for constitutionality despite Cabinet certification.
